anchor.title: La Città Leonina
anchor.text: Nell'846 una flotta saracena risale il Tevere e saccheggia San Pietro, che sorge fuori dalle mura di Roma; i razziatori strappano l'argento dalla tomba dell'apostolo. In risposta papa Leone IV fa cingere l'intero quartiere vaticano da un muro fortificato, alto dodici metri con torri rotonde, consacrato nell'852. Il distretto racchiuso diventa la Città Leonina, il primo Vaticano cinto da mura.

meanwhile.title: The last date
meanwhile.text: Tikal’s last known dated stela carries a Long Count date equivalent to 869 CE. Over the following decades the city’s royal institutions and population decline sharply, part of the wider political transformation of the southern Maya lowlands; drought, warfare, environmental stress and political fragmentation are all studied as contributing factors.

meanwhile.title: The settlement of Tuvalu
meanwhile.text: Voyagers from Samoa and Tonga settle Tuvalu's low coral islands. They bring crops, animals, and navigation traditions, and each island preserves founding voyages through oral genealogy.

meanwhile.title: Island Caribs
meanwhile.text: Kalinago communities are established across Grenada and the southern Lesser Antilles before sustained European colonization. They travel widely by canoe for fishing, trade and warfare and resist repeated European attempts to settle the island.

meanwhile.title: The Afar of the Danakil
meanwhile.text: Afar-speaking pastoral communities have long lived across the arid lands of present-day Djibouti, Eritrea and Ethiopia. Livestock herding, salt trading and control of wells and caravan routes shape regional livelihoods, while political authority is organized through changing clan and sultanate structures.

meanwhile.title: The seafaring Manteño
meanwhile.text: Along the central coast, the Manteño build trading societies whose balsa rafts carry Spondylus shell and other goods over long stretches of the Pacific.

meanwhile.title: The Abbasid town of Murwab
meanwhile.text: Inland from the northwest coast a town of some 250 houses, two mosques and a fort spreads across the desert under the Abbasid caliphate. Copper coins and glazed Basra ware tie it to the empire's trade. It is abandoned within a century, parts of it burned, the largest early-Islamic settlement yet excavated in Qatar.
